findings.reason: naming the two prior digests converts "new machinery" into "generalize the existing source-digest helper", which is the cheaper and more honest change.
findings.text: §3 designs a canonical source digest (whitespace-stable hash over the LinkML source files, not the graph contents) as if new, but that is exactly the shape already implemented twice: `grammar_content_digest()` at imas_codex/standard_names/grammar_sync.py:144 (canonical YAML→JSON → sha256, mtime-signature cached at grammar_sync.py:94-170, persisted as `ISNGrammarVersion.content_digest` and consulted by the startup autosync at imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1338), and the prompt-template digest at imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.py:1275-1313; the plan names neither, so its §2 claim that this is "the missing third member" omits that the member already has two working implementations to follow or generalize.

findings.reason: the plan should either generalize the existing digest mechanism (parameterize its input paths) or state why it cannot, rather than add a third implementation.
findings.text: §5 proposes a schema-digest layer writing a node "in the same shape as DDVersion" plus a connect-time comparison, but gives no statement of why `grammar_content_digest()` (grammar_sync.py:144) and its startup freshness comparison cannot be extended to the LinkML sources; a second, parallel digest-and-store path over the same idea is a wrapper over existing machinery with no justification for not extending it.

findings.reason: naming the owning file lets the digest be written at the single point the schema is applied, instead of a second writer that drifts from it.
findings.text: the plan says the digest is "written as a node when the schema is applied" but names no owner: `GraphClient.initialize_schema()` / `_initialize_schema_impl()` (client.py:331,358) is the mechanism that reads the LinkML schema (`GraphSchema(schema_path="imas_codex/schemas/imas_dd.yaml")`) and applies the graph schema, and the LinkML source set it would digest is already enumerated at scripts/gen_schema_context.py:38-46 (facility.yaml, common.yaml, imas_dd.yaml, standard_name.yaml, task_groups.yaml); a new placement path forks the one place the schema is applied. The same census applies to the digest itself: the owners to extend, not parallelize, are grammar_sync.py:144 and prompt_loader.py:1275.

findings.reason: the section must account for the new refusal family and node type in its own text — by naming what it retires or by stating why nothing can be.
findings.text: §5 adds surface in two of the tracked families: a refusal family (the server refuses to serve on digest mismatch) and a new node type for the digest, yet the section names nothing it retires or merges and gives no reason nothing can be; the server already carries a refusal precedent (`_refuse_governed_standard_name_write` at imas_codex/llm/server.py:130) and a health surface (imas_codex/llm/server.py:3780) that the new refusal could extend rather than augment.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design is one small module hiding a modest behaviour (compute a source digest, persist it as a node, compare it on connect) behind a small interface; there is no spread of shallow wrappers over one mechanism to unwrap.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements digest-over-source and the "written when the schema is applied" placement without naming the owners to extend (`grammar_sync.py:144`, `prompt_loader.py:1275`, `client.py:331`, `scripts/gen_schema_context.py:38`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §5 adds a server refusal family and a new node type without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the `DDVersion`/`ISNGrammarVersion` version *nodes* and `schema_context_data.py`, but never names `grammar_content_digest()` (`imas_codex/standard_names/grammar_sync.py:144`) or the prompt `source_digest` (`imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.py:1275`), the two source-digest mechanisms it would replicate.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan adds a schema digest plus a connect-time check as a fresh layer paralleling the existing `ISNGrammarVersion.content_digest` mechanism, and states no reason that machinery cannot be generalized instead.
